en: The Philippines is an archipelago consisting of exactly 7,641 islands during high tide.
Mount Apo in Davao is the highest peak in the Philippines, reaching an elevation of 2,954 meters above sea level.
The Cagayan River is the longest river in the Philippines, stretching approximately 505 kilometers from the Caraballo Mountains to the Pacific Ocean.
Laguna de Bay is the largest lake in the Philippines, covering a surface area of about 911 square kilometers.
Leyte Gulf is the largest bay in the Philippines, covering a massive water surface area of roughly 3,800 square kilometers.
Taal Volcano in Batangas is one of the most active volcanoes in the Philippines, having erupted over 30 times in recorded history.
The Sierra Madre is the longest mountain range in the Philippines, stretching approximately 540 kilometers along the eastern coast of Luzon.
The Puerto Princesa Subterranean River features a navigable underground river stretching 8.2 kilometers long through a massive limestone cave in Palawan.
The Philippine tarsier, one of the world's smallest primates at just 85 to 160 millimeters tall, is native to Bohol.
The Northern Sierra Madre Natural Park is the largest protected area in the Philippines, encompassing roughly 364,636 hectares of intact tropical rainforest.
The Philippines has a highly indented coastline measuring approximately 36,289 kilometers long, ranking among the longest coastlines in the world.
The Philippine Trench reaches a maximum depth of 10,540 meters, making it the deepest oceanic trench in the Philippine Sea.
